title: Rabbi Chinena bar Yitzchak
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman finds him mentioned only in the Jerusalem Talmud and the Midrashim, in aggadah. In Berakhot 6:1, folio 39b: “Rabbi Chinena bar Yitzchak and Rabbi Shmuel bar Imi — one said: The turnip was not bread,” etc. In Taanit 2:4: “Rabbi Chunah in the name of Rabbi Chinena bar Yitzchak: All that day Abraham saw the ram,” etc. Likewise in Vayikra Rabbah 10:5 and Midrash Tehillim 100:20, Rabbi Hunah in his name. The statement in Bereshit Rabbah 22:13 has “Rabbi Chama in his name,” and Hyman proposes Rabbi Huna. He is likewise mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah 41:6: “Rabbi Chanina son of Rabbi Yitzchak said: It is not written ve’asme’alah here but ve’asme’ilah — from every place I will turn left (which Hyman regards as the plain intent of the verse).” There, 56:9, he said: “All the days of the year,” etc. There, 8:11, 14:3 and 37:2, Rabbi Yehoshua bar Nechemyah in his name. In Kohelet Rabbah 1:9: “Rabbi Chanina bar Yitzchak said: It is written mikaran” — Hyman proposes Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak. In Esther Rabbah, beginning of chapter 3: “Rabbi Chanina bar Yitzchak said: Honor yourself,” etc. In Tanchuma, Vayishlach 2, he said: “Fortunate is the one born of woman who heard so from his Creator.” In Midrash Tehillim 90:15 he said: “Even his royal house (of David) is toil and iniquity.” There, 90:16, he said: “Whoever first experiences suffering in this world has a share in the world to come.” In Tanchuma, Toledot 23, he is mentioned as Rabbi Chananyah bar Yitzchak. He is likewise mentioned in Kohelet Rabbah 1:12.

notes.text: לפת is turnip, with a play on לא פת, not a statement that bread was not bread: saved Guggenheimer JTBerakhot6:1 paragraph8 contains both forms. Hyman’s proposed רנב״י expansion as Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak is supported by the parallel full name in saved Davidson Shabbat28b paragraph6, while the saved ToratEmet KoheletRabbah1:9 still reads Chanina bar Yitzchak. Hyman’s Huna/Chama and other name variants remain scoped proposals, not corrections of a printed witness.

Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:1 directly names Chinena bar Yitzchak and Shmuel bar Imi in the turnip/not-bread wordplay. Other incidental Yitzchak matches in the same chapter were excluded. Hyman’s Kohelet Nachman correction and Huna/Chama alternatives are not imposed on the consulted printed witness; the retained current note distinguishes the Shabbat parallel.
